messages.subject: Re: Leave-one-out cross-validation in lavaan
parts:
On 12/03/2015 04:24 PM, Christin Scholz wrote:
> then uses the estimates to predict
> the last case using lavPredict() (which is similar to predict() but has
> more options for SEM).

Oh dear. Another victim of the 'predict()' confusion. In 0.5-19, I
expanded the documentation of lavPredict() a bit, and I added to the
'details' section the following:

"If there are no latent variables in the model, ‘type = "ov"’ will
simply return the values of the observed variables. Note that this
function can not be used to `predict' values of dependent
variables, given the values of independent values (in the
regression sense). In other words, the structural component is
completely ignored (for now)."

Example:

> fit <- sem('y1 ~ x1 + x2; y2 ~ y1', data = PoliticalDemocracy)
> head( lavPredict(fit, type="yhat") )
y1 y2 x1 x2
[1,] 2.50 0.000000 4.442651 3.637586
[2,] 1.25 0.000000 5.384495 5.062595
[3,] 7.50 8.800000 5.961005 6.255750
[4,] 8.90 8.800000 6.285998 7.567863
[5,] 10.00 3.333333 5.863631 6.818924
[6,] 7.50 3.333333 5.533389 5.135798

> head( PoliticalDemocracy[,c("y1","y2","x1","x2")] )
y1 y2 x1 x2
1 2.50 0.000000 4.442651 3.637586
2 1.25 0.000000 5.384495 5.062595
3 7.50 8.800000 5.961005 6.255750
4 8.90 8.800000 6.285998 7.567863
5 10.00 3.333333 5.863631 6.818924
6 7.50 3.333333 5.533389 5.135798

The very purpose of lavPredict() is to `predict' latent variable scores
(aka factor scores). It is (currently) not very useful in the
observed-variables-only setting.

In the latent variable setting, the purpose of type="ov" (or
type="yhat") is to compute the model-implied (continuous) values for the
observed indicators, once we have computed the model-implied latent
variable scores.

If you need predictions in the regression sense, you will need to
compute them manually.

Yves.
